players.name: Marcus Zelee
players.route: Austin Achieve → Brentwood Christian → Austin Prep Academy → UNT
players.bio: A Texas freshman who earned first-team all-state recognition at Austin Prep and helped it reach the TCAL championship game. Earlier stops included Brentwood Christian and Austin Achieve. His official bio lists ASAK Elite as his club program.
players.cue: Track the first pass after he crosses half court. Does it create movement or leave everyone standing?

players.name: Cash Chavis
players.route: Park Center HS → Arkansas → UT Arlington → UNT
players.bio: A transfer point guard who started all 34 games for UT Arlington in 2025–26, averaging 10.5 points and 3.5 assists. He helped Park Center win a Minnesota state title and also played wide receiver. UNT’s cumulative table credits him with six steals against Santa Clara; the recap’s prose and scoring table disagree on his points, so the statistical table is used here.
players.cue: Watch how he attacks a passing lane without losing his assignment. Does the steal lead to a controlled possession?

clips.title: Cash Chavis · senior high-school highlights
clips.context: Park Center footage, before his college career. Historical highlights, not current UNT game film.

players.name: EJ Horton
players.bio: A returning guard who appeared in 30 games last season and earned an American Conference Freshman of the Week award. His official bio highlights a road win at Temple with 12 points, five steals and four rebounds. The current three-game cumulative table does not include him; that alone is not an injury diagnosis.
players.cue: Follow his defense for three possessions: where does he stand before the ball reaches his man?

players.name: Amar Amkou
players.route: CSI Keur Madior → Florida Atlantic → UNT
players.bio: A Senegalese guard with unusual size for the position. At Florida Atlantic he appeared in 26 games in 2025–26, shot 36.4 percent from three and recorded a 10-point, 10-rebound double-double against Saint Leo. He made four threes against UNT before transferring to Denton.
players.cue: Look for the matchup he creates: is a smaller defender guarding him, or is a forward chasing him outside?

players.name: Je’Shawn Stevenson
players.bio: The American Conference’s preseason player of the year. He followed Robinson from Cleveland State, where he was Horizon League Freshman of the Year, and averaged 17.3 points in his first UNT season. A Lindblom graduate and the school’s career scoring leader, he opened this year with a career-best 30 against McNeese.
players.cue: Watch the defender who leaves a teammate to help on his drive. Who becomes available for the next pass?

players.name: Braylon Barnes
players.bio: A junior-college transfer who started all 34 games for Jones College and averaged 16.8 points. He made 62 threes, earned all-conference recognition and helped the Bobcats reach the NJCAA national tournament. His official bio describes 28 double-figure scoring games in that season.
players.cue: After he passes, does he relocate into a clean shooting window? Watch his feet before the catch.

players.name: Filip Kalajzic
players.bio: A Croatian newcomer with club experience in Croatia and Slovenia. His official bio records 13.7 points, 7.9 rebounds and 1.9 blocks for Gorica, plus appearances for Croatia at the 2023 FIBA U20 European Championship. The roster labels him a freshman; that does not mean he is new to high-level basketball.
players.cue: Watch his positioning before a rebound. Can he seal an opponent away from the ball rather than simply jump higher?

players.name: Cole Franklin
players.bio: A returning senior with a Texas homecoming story and prior experience under Robinson at Cleveland State. He played every game last season and started 23. His official bio lists career highs of 21 points, ten rebounds and six steals. The opening-week preview singled out his rebounding and steals against Santa Clara a year earlier.
players.cue: Watch the possessions where he does not shoot. Which screen, rotation or rebound makes him useful?

players.name: Aeneas Alexander
players.bio: A local freshman who played for former NBA guard Raymond Felton at Pace Academy. His Nike ProSkills U17 team finished fourth at Peach Jam in 2025. He chose UNT from a group of Division I offers and immediately became an early contributor off the bench.
players.cue: Does his length help on the offensive glass, and can he stay spaced when the ball goes inside?

players.name: Mitchell Holmes
players.bio: A Fort Worth big man arriving from SMU. His official biography records 26 appearances in 2025–26, a 70.4 percent field-goal mark in limited minutes and ten points in an 11-minute outing against Butler. He is on UNT’s current roster but not in the reviewed three-game cumulative table; no current absence is independently confirmed.
players.cue: Watch how he creates a target for the entry pass and whether he can turn a screen into a useful roll.

players.name: Reece Robinson
players.bio: A returning forward and Daniyal Robinson’s son. He earned Horizon League All-Freshman honors at Cleveland State and academic all-district recognition at UNT. His official biography lists a 23-point game at Charlotte last season. Against Santa Clara this November he scored 15, with eleven before halftime.
players.cue: Follow the cut that happens before he gets the ball. Is he exploiting a defender who has turned to help?

players.name: TJ Crumble
players.bio: A first-year forward from Cleveland by way of Long Island Lutheran. The current official player page supplies little extended biography, so his background is limited here to verified roster information. His first three appearances are a very small sample, not a settled description of his role.
players.cue: Watch his first defensive assignment after checking in and how quickly he finds the team’s spacing.

players.name: Ousmane Ndour
players.bio: A Senegalese forward whose route to Denton includes Spain. His official bio lists a redshirt season in 2025–26. This November he has become an interior contributor, with eleven offensive rebounds in three games and an 18-point outing against Santa Clara.
players.cue: Watch the second effort after a missed shot: does he create a new possession before anyone thinks about scoring?

coaches.name: Daniyal Robinson
coaches.bio: A Rock Island, Illinois native in his second season at UNT. He inherited a complete roster turnover, then went 19–14 in 2025–26. At Cleveland State he produced three consecutive 20-win seasons. His staff history links Little Rock, Illinois State, Iowa State, Houston and Loyola Chicago.
playing: 1995–96 · Indian Hills CC (season verified in Houston bio)
career: 2013–15 · Loyola Chicago · assistant / associate head coach

coaches.name: Kwanza Johnson
coaches.bio: A former Tulsa captain whose teams reached consecutive Sweet 16s. He earned economics and law degrees at Tulsa before building a coaching career across major conferences and mid-major programs. He worked with Robinson at Cleveland State before joining UNT in April 2025.
playing: Before 1993 · Rose State College · exact seasons not listed

coaches.name: Steve Payne
coaches.bio: A veteran of more than thirty years in college coaching, including eight as Tennessee Tech’s head coach. His career includes a Texas junior-college head job and work with Robinson at Cleveland State. He joined UNT in May 2025.
playing: Playing years are not specified in the current UNT biography.
1990 · Union College bachelor’s degree (education, not a verified playing tenure)

coaches.name: Deshon Parker
coaches.bio: A former Robinson player who moved from professional basketball into coaching. Across his college career he played 150 games and passed 1,000 points. His final Cleveland State season earned Horizon All-Defensive honors; a season in Georgia followed before he joined Robinson’s staff.
playing: Through 2022–23 · College career · 150 games, 126 starts; earlier years not detailed here

coaches.name: Mo Ba
coaches.bio: His pathway centers on player development, video and scouting. He worked with Houston’s 2021 Final Four team, spent two years at Iowa State, then worked in the Milwaukee Bucks’ player-development operation. He reunited with Robinson at Cleveland State and joined UNT in April 2025.
playing: A competitive playing career is not specified in the reviewed UNT bio.
career: 2021–23 · Iowa State · assistant director of player development
2024–25 · Cleveland State · director of player development

coaches.name: Cole Christian
coaches.bio: Hired in June 2026, Christian brings offensive coordination, scouting and analytics experience. He previously worked with Robinson at Iowa State. His appointment report describes responsibility for offensive systems at Murray State and South Dakota State; it supplies the career detail missing from his roster bio.
playing: Through 2017 · Iowa State · student manager / marketing degree
career: 2025–26 · South Dakota State · assistant (appointment prose; its summary list shortens the school name)

quote.text: a relentless worker, a tremendous basketball mind
quote.by: Daniyal Robinson on Cole Christian · June 5, 2026
